title: Gul Mohammad v. U.P. Power Corporation and 2 Others
coram: Sunil Ambwani, J. & Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of relegating the consumer to the Clause 6.5(b) mechanism, with recovery under the 1957 Dues Recovery Act stayed pending the representation
headnote: A consumer disputing the accuracy of a bill must invoke the self-contained mechanism of Clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 - paying under protest either the sum claimed or the charges computed on the average of the preceding six months' bills (whichever is less) and filing a complaint with the competent authority, to be decided within seven days. Where a running bill of Rs. 2,761 was allegedly inflated to a demand of Rs. 74,424 under Section 3 of the U.P. Electricity (Undertaking) Dues Recovery Act, 1957, the Court disposed of the writ directing that, if the consumer files a representation and deposits the six-month-average charges, it be decided within seven days, and stayed recovery under the demand notice until then.

holding_units.clause: 6.5(b) (r/w s.3, U.P. Electricity (Undertaking) Dues Recovery Act, 1957)
holding_units.topic: Bill-accuracy dispute pursued via the Clause 6.5(b) pay-under-protest-and-complain mechanism; recovery stayed
holding_units.question: Where a bill is alleged to be grossly inflated and recovery is threatened under the 1957 Dues Recovery Act, what is the consumer's remedy?
holding_units.holding: Clause 6.5(b) provides the remedy: the consumer may pay under protest either the sum claimed or the six-month-average charges (whichever is less) and complain to the competent authority (here the Executive Engineer / respondent no. 2), the complaint to be decided within seven days. The Court directed that, on such a representation with deposit of the six-month-average charges, it be decided within seven days, and stayed recovery under the demand notice until its disposal.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Running bill of Rs. 2,761 allegedly inflated to a Rs. 74,424 demand under s.3 of the 1957 Dues Recovery Act; consumer (successor of deceased father) paying bills; competent authority identified.

principle_tags.application: A grossly-inflated-bill grievance is to be pursued through the Clause 6.5(b) pay-under-protest-and-complain mechanism, with recovery stayed pending decision.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand of Rs. 74,424 was correctly computed
not_decided.note: Left to the competent authority on the Clause 6.5(b) complaint.
